zh.title: 美國新建一條機場跑道要多少錢？從1億到11億美元的代價
zh.summary: 美國新建商用機場跑道動輒1億至11億美元，土地、環評、土方與聯邦補助規定層層推高造價；翻修雖便宜卻無法增加容量，平行跑道仍是唯一永久解方。
body: 在美國新建一條商用機場跑道，總造價通常介於1億美元至11億美元以上，取決於場地條件、土地徵收與工程規模。以北卡羅來納州羅利—達拉姆國際機場為例，全長10639英尺（3242公尺）的新跑道5L-23R，整體計畫預算約11億美元；阿斯本／皮特金郡機場的機場與航廈整體現代化計畫，預算也約2.69億美元。單就鋪面工程而言，每英里造價約2600萬至4200萬美元以上，視鋪面厚度、路肩與燈光複雜度而定，但鋪面合約只是總帳單的一小部分。

成本推手首先來自土地與環境：全新選址工程在澆灌高強度混凝土之前，就要支付土地徵收、環境緩解、遷移道路與管線的費用；土方與整地往往占初期預算極大比重，商用跑道須採用P-501混凝土或深層P-401瀝青，以承受超過100萬磅（453592公斤）的輪載，地下管線、高強度LED燈具與精密導航設備又要再花費數百萬美元。機場基建通膨長期高於一般物價，主因是美國聯邦航空總署嚴格的材料規格與品管檢測；許多機場因此仰賴聯邦補助，例如機場改善計畫與《兩黨基礎建設法》下的機場基建補助，阿斯本機場近期就獲得3700萬美元補助。

預算超支也十分常見：施工團隊常遇到未預見的地下水或回填土，必須花錢整治；希臘羅得斯迪亞戈拉斯國際機場就因跑道下方地下水問題多次關閉維修，類似情況下最終造價經常比預估高出兩位數百分比。相較之下，跑道翻修等替代方案便宜得多，卻無法增加起降容量；新建平行跑道是唯一能永久紓解壅塞的辦法，但徵地、遷路與環評往往讓動工前置期拉長5至10年。小型通用航空機場若只延長跑道400英尺（122公尺），在土質良好、環評單純的情況下，投資可能僅需300萬至600萬美元，與大型樞紐擴建完全不同。

en.title: How much does a new airport runway cost in the US in 2026?
en.summary: A new commercial airport runway in the US typically costs $100 million to over $1.1 billion, driven by land, environmental review, earthwork and FAA standards; rehabilitation is cheaper but cannot add capacity.
body: Building a brand-new commercial airport runway in the United States typically costs from $100 million to upwards of $1.1 billion, heavily dictated by site conditions, land acquisition and scale. Raleigh-Durham International Airport's new 10,639-foot (3,242-metre) Runway 5L-23R carries a total program budget of approximately $1.1 billion, while the comprehensive airfield and terminal modernization program at Aspen/Pitkin County Airport is budgeted at approximately $269 million. Basic airfield paving contracts alone run from roughly $26 million to over $42 million per mile, depending on pavement thickness, shoulder requirements and lighting complexity, yet a paving contract is only a fraction of the total bill.

Greenfield projects require major spending on land acquisition, environmental mitigation and relocating roadways or utility grids before any high-strength concrete is laid. Earthwork and site grading frequently consume large shares of the initial budget, and commercial runways need high-strength P-501 concrete or deep-section P-401 asphalt engineered to withstand rolling gear loads exceeding 1,000,000 lb (453,592 kilograms), as noted by ICAO. Underground utility routing, high-intensity LED lighting and precision navigational aids add millions more. Airport infrastructure inflation has consistently outpaced consumer price growth, driven by the Federal Aviation Administration's strict material specifications and quality-control testing, so many airports rely heavily on federal support such as the FAA's Airport Improvement Program and Airport Infrastructure Grants funded through the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law; Aspen received a recent $37 million AIP grant.

Budgets also routinely overrun. Engineering teams frequently encounter unforeseen groundwater or subsurface fill requiring expensive remediation, and at Rhodes Diagoras International Airport, groundwater under the runway led to repeated closures and repairs, while final costs routinely exceed initial estimates by double-digit percentages. Cheaper alternatives exist: full-depth pavement rehabilitation or mill-and-overlay resurfacing costs a fraction of greenfield construction, but cannot increase aircraft movement capacity once all slots are used. A parallel runway is the only permanent solution for simultaneous arrival and departure delays, yet acquiring adjacent land, relocating roads and completing environmental reviews can add five to ten years of pre-construction lead time. Small exceptions exist: a regional airstrip extending a runway by 400 feet (122 metres) might need only $3 million to $6 million if soil conditions are favourable and environmental clearances are straightforward.

facts.claim: A new commercial airport runway in the United States typically costs from $100 million to upwards of $1.1 billion, depending on site conditions, land acquisition and scale.

Raleigh-Durham International Airport's new 10,639-foot Runway 5L-23R has a total program budget of approximately $1.1 billion, and Aspen/Pitkin County Airport's airfield and terminal modernization is budgeted at approximately $269 million.

Commercial runways require P-501 concrete or P-401 asphalt engineered to withstand rolling gear loads exceeding 1,000,000 lb (453,592 kg), and airports rely on federal support such as the FAA Airport Improvement Program; Aspen received a $37 million AIP grant.

Unexpected groundwater or subsurface conditions can push final costs double-digit percentages above estimates, as at Rhodes Diagoras International Airport, while a parallel runway can require five to ten years of pre-construction lead time.
